title: Wave width and sandbox capacity stop being two numbers
description:
One sandbox per tick instead of four subprocesses in one container makes concurrency a factory-level limit rather than a container-level one, and the limit is currently written down twice: max_instances is 3, and the dispatch width has its own copy of that number in wrangler.toml.

Two numbers that must agree and are maintained separately will drift, and the failure when they do is a wave that dispatches more ticks than the factory can host - which surfaces as sandbox creation failures attributed to whichever tick happened to be fourth, not as a capacity message.

Make one of them the source and derive or check the other. A startup check that refuses to boot on disagreement is an acceptable answer and is better than a comment asking people to keep them in sync.
